描述_EN: camels and horses were used as pack animals and merchants passed their goods from oasis to oasis. the victoria and albert museum has around 700 ancient and medieval textiles recovered by stein at the beginning of the twentieth century. this object was brought back from central asia by the explorer and archaeologist sir marc aurel stein (1862–1943). the most notable item traded was silk. the site is part of an area now referred to as the silk road, a series of overland trade routes that crossed asia, from china to europe. the silk road was also important for the exchange of ideas – while silk textiles travelled west from china, buddhism entered china from india in this way. its original purpose is unclear although it is likely to have been used as a pouch. it was recovered from the site of miran fort on the eastern verge of the taklamakan desert. many textile fragments were discovered here in the remains of a fort held by the tibetans during their domination of the southern taklamakan in the 8th century ad. some are silk while others are made from the wool of a variety of different animals. this textile piece, which has been folded over and stitched, is of pattern woven silk. the textiles range in date from the second century bc to the twelfth century ad.
描述_ZN: 年，骆驼和马被用作驮运动物，商人们在绿洲之间传递他们的货物。 年，维多利亚和阿尔伯特博物馆有大约700件古代和中世纪的纺织品，是斯坦在20世纪初找到的。 年，这个物品被探险家和考古学家Marc Aurel Stein先生（1862-1943）从中亚带回来。 年，最引人注目的贸易项目是丝绸。 年：该遗址是现在被称为 "丝绸之路 "的地区的一部分，这是一系列横跨亚洲、从中国到欧洲的陆上贸易路线。 年：丝绸之路对思想交流也很重要--当丝绸纺织品从中国向西运输时，佛教也通过这种方式从印度进入中国。 其原始用途不清楚，尽管它可能被用作一个袋子。 它是在塔克拉玛干沙漠东部边缘的Miran堡垒遗址上发现的。 许多纺织品碎片是在公元8世纪西藏人统治塔克拉玛干南部期间的堡垒遗址中发现的。 有些是丝绸，有些则是由各种不同动物的羊毛制成。 这块被折叠和缝合的纺织品是用丝绸编织的图案。 这些纺织品的年代从公元前二世纪到公元十二世纪不等。
